lines.text: Why is the sea salty, when the rivers that fill it taste fresh?
Rain is slightly acidic. It wears down rock, and rivers carry the dissolved minerals to the sea.
Then the sun lifts the water back into the sky. The salt stays behind.
Repeat that for billions of years, and every litre of seawater holds about thirty-five grams of salt.
The rivers are salty too. Just too little to taste.
